s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of chest pain, palpitations, and shortness of breath with hypotension, tachycardia, and tachypnea, suggesting a cardiovascular emergency
salient_findings: Anterior-wall hypokinesia and moderate-to-severe aortic insufficiency
key_facts: 47-year-old woman
Presented with crescendo chest pain, palpitations, and shortness of breath
Hypotensive, tachycardic, and tachypneic
Bilateral fine basal crepitations on physical examination
Grade 2 decrescendo diastolic murmur
Bilateral pitting lower-limb edema
Active smoker
No history of substance misuse or family history of cardiovascular disease
Chest radiography showed congested basal lung fields with mild bilateral pleural effusions
Electrocardiography showed ST-segment depressions in the inferior leads
Transthoracic echocardiography revealed anterior-wall hypokinesia and moderate-to-severe aortic insufficiency
Immobile echogenic shadows in the ascending aorta obscured the aortic valve

per_call: Myxomatous degeneration of the aortic valve

shortlist.label: Syphilitic aortitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with aortic insufficiency and atypical findings prompted investigations for infectious aortitis, with Treponema pallidum being a potential causative organism

shortlist.label: Takayasu arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and sex, combined with the presence of aortic insufficiency and atypical findings, make this large vessel vasculitis a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Aortic valve endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Immobile echogenic shadows in the ascending aorta obscured the aortic valve, raising suspicion for endocarditis, particularly in the context of aortic insufficiency

shortlist.label: Acute aortic dissection
shortlist.why_kept: Although the computed tomography aortogram excluded aortic dissection, the patient's presentation with chest pain, hypotension, and tachycardia warrants consideration of this life-threatening condition

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal aortitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with aortic insufficiency and atypical findings, combined with the consideration of infectious aortitis, makes Staphylococcus species a potential causative organism

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with aortic insufficiency, immobile echogenic shadows in the ascending aorta, and the exclusion of other causes such as aortic dissection, along with the consideration of Treponema pallidum as a potential causative organism, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Takayasu arteritis
rejected.why: No evidence of musculoskeletal or immunological findings suggestive of this condition

rejected.label: Aortic valve endocarditis
rejected.why: The presence of immobile echogenic shadows in the ascending aorta rather than on the valve itself makes this less likely

rejected.label: Staphylococcal aortitis
rejected.why: While possible, the combination of findings and the specific consideration of Treponema pallidum makes Syphilitic aortitis a more fitting diagnosis
